item.title: Glass House / Charlene Koetz Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The Glass House (Casa de Vidro) was conceived from a contemporary architecture of strong horizontal expression, where the lightness of the planes and the precision of the lines define a sophisticated and timeless aesthetic. The large cantilevered roof plane, a striking element of the project, seems to float over the volumes, creating wide protected areas and reinforcing the feeling of shelter. In contrast, the natural stone volumes bring solidity and anchor the building to the ground, while the glazed surfaces take center stage, dissolving the boundaries between interior and exterior and establishing a direct and permanent connection with the landscape. This balanced relationship between transparency and mass results in an architecture that values nature as an essential part of the living experience.

item.title: Portola Valley Home / Schwartz and Architecture
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: To add a bit of surprise to what otherwise could be a standard ranch house façade, we wanted the updated 'face' of this home to feel as if it were suddenly coming alive and welcoming you as you approach.

item.title: Green House / M2 Senos Arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Pilar Caballero
item.description: Casa Verde is located in Costa Nova do Prado, a Portuguese Atlantic beach famous for its “palheiros”—originally storage buildings used in fishing, which over generations transformed into colorful striped houses, delighting the holidaymakers lucky enough to pass through.

item.title: Radically Collective: The Legacy of Cuba's Microbrigadas Housing Program
item.dc:creator: Moises Carrasco
item.description: In the 1970s, Cuba faced a severe nationwide housing shortage due to population growth, rural-to-urban migration, and the degradation of existing housing stock. The government's answer was a system that pulled ordinary workers off their regular jobs and put them on building sites instead. This program, known as the Microbrigadas (microbrigades), reshaped entire districts of Havana, where they combined collective self-construction and state-backed technical knowledge, which left a mark on the urban grid of its capital city that persists until today.

item.title: Bidi Bidi Performing Arts Centre / To​.org + Hassell + Localworks + Arup
item.dc:creator: Miwa Negoro
item.description: A place for cultural expression, collaboration and community, Bidi Bidi Performing Arts Centre is a thriving beacon of creativity and unity in Africa's largest refugee settlement. Bidi Bidi Performing Arts Centre, northern Uganda, is the result of a collaboration led by creative platform To​.org, in partnership with Hassell, architecture practice LocalWorks, and design and engineering firm Arup, to create a community hub that empowers creativity, creates opportunity and brings dignity to the plight of refugees.

item.title: What Is the Right Wood for Outdoor Use?
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Selecting wood for outdoor applications involves more than appearance alone. Durability, stability, versatility and sustainability all influence how a material performs over time. Understanding these factors can help architects, builders and homeowners choose the right wood for exterior projects.

item.title: Donald Judd’s Artillery Sheds in Texas to Undergo Major Restoration
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: The Chinati Foundation has announced plans to restore the Artillery Sheds in Marfa, Texas, the former military buildings adapted by artist Donald Judd to house his 100 untitled works in mill aluminum, created between 1982 and 1986. Led by architect Troy Schaum of Schaum Architects, the multi-year preservation project is being developed with the Getty Conservation Institute and will address the historic buildings' envelope, accessibility, environmental performance, and landscape while preserving Judd's site-specific installation. The project follows the Artillery Sheds' inclusion in the National Register of Historic Places in 2025 as part of the expanded Donald Judd Historic District.

item.title: Cabin Sande / Helen & Hard architects
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The site of Cabin Sande is defined by the vast horizon over the Atlantic Ocean, the dark and rough rocky landscape descending toward the sea, and the untouched natural vegetation in the rear part of the property. Our aim was to create an architecture that connects these distinct landscape zones while establishing a strong relationship with the site's inherent qualities.

item.title: OMA/AMO and OPEN Architecture Design Opening Exhibitions for Powerhouse Parramatta in Sydney, Australia
item.dc:creator: Antonia Piñeiro
item.description: Powerhouse Parramatta, a new museum and cultural institution on the banks of the Parramatta River in Western Sydney, Australia, will open to the public on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The 30,000-square-meter building has been designed by Franco-Japanese firm Moreau Kusunoki as lead designer, with Australian firm Genton as local architect and Arup as engineer. Moreau Kusunoki won the design competition for the project in 2019, with completion initially planned for 2025. Powerhouse Parramatta is the first state cultural organization located in Western Sydney, a region whose population includes communities from more than 170 countries. At opening, the museum will present five exhibitions.

item.title: From Selecting to Making: When Architects Become Material Producers
item.dc:creator: Daniela Andino
item.description: Architects are trained to choose materials, compare their properties, and decide how they should be used. Some practices are taking on a different task: developing the material itself.

item.title: Gochang Hwang Yunseok Library / Hyunjoon Yoo + Partners
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Thanks to the digital environment, we can now easily access knowledge and information anytime, anywhere. So what significance do public libraries have today? They act as a living room for everyone, a place where anyone can stay, relax, and create memories for free.

item.title: Twilight House / Spacefiction Studio
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Uprooting into the future – The client wanted to move his parents from their ancestral home to a nature-centric, designed one. The program was to fit more rooms for the children and grandchildren, so they could stay comfortably on their visits, which their current home lacked. The more people age, the more they are rooted in their environment, habits, and ways.

item.title: A Leaf Canopy by the Sea / Studio 10
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: The project sits on a tree-lined grassy slope along the coast of Shenzhen Bay Park, one of the city's most popular public parks. The site boasts abundant wildlife and serves as a resting ground for Siberian migratory birds flying south. Centered on a "light intervention" design philosophy, the scheme strikes a subtle balance between public space, park-based retail and ecological conservation.

item.title: Abejas Sports and Recreation Center / border arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The Abejas Sports and Recreation Center in Tijuana explores the role architecture can play in improving everyday life in underserved areas. Developed within a neighborhood shaped by rapid urban growth and limited access to quality public infrastructure, the project introduces a space dedicated to sports, recreation, and community activity.

item.title: House in Santana do Parnaíba / GRUPOSP
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Located in Santana do Parnaíba, this residence establishes an intentional dialogue with the landscape, orienting itself to take advantage of the privileged view of the woods in the adjacent valley, which is fully integrated into its living areas.

item.title: HUB UCC. Universidad Católica de Córdoba Innovation Space / BLT Arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The Universidad Católica de Córdoba operates on a campus that, following the traditional format, originally assigned a building to each academic unit or field of study. In a contemporary world that demands interdisciplinary research and design dynamics, architecture must transcend fragmentation to enhance collective life and foster social cohesion within the academic community. This requires more flexible spaces that, rather than functioning as isolated compartments, encourage the intersection of disciplines and ideas to foster innovation and the development of new projects. The architecture of the hub makes room for what is yet unknown, for innovation, creation, and the materialization of ideas, and for the interdisciplinary convergence of the university community.

item.title: House on the Northern Coast of Sao Paulo / André Vainer Arquitetos
item.dc:creator: Valeria Silva
item.description: Designed for six siblings and their families, this spacious seafront house occupies a corner lot in a housing development tract designed by the brilliant Lúcio Costa. The generous scale of the house called for an L-shaped layout, which allows most of the rooms to face both the sea and the pool and garden enclosed within the site. A separate caretaker’s house is located near the street entrance. Built on a previously filled site, the house stretches in a long, linear form between the required setbacks imposed by local building regulations.

item.title: 90/100 Mixed Use Project / 5468796 Architecture
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: On a long parcel at the edge of Winnipeg's East Exchange District, 90/100, named for its address, unites a 1905 warehouse with a seven-storey contemporary volume to create a medium-density, mixed-use development. Containing 206 residential suites spanning new and old buildings and 6000 square feet of commercial space, the project establishes a deliberate counterpoint to the area's conventional, opaque residential buildings through careful choreography of massing, open space and glazing, rendering the building physically and symbolically open. It strikes a rare balance contributing to the urban fabric, establishing a landmark distinguished by bold geometry and material precision.

item.title: Finishing
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Obra Blanca is an essential experience for professionals in the architecture finishes and design products sector, including ceramics, bathroom furniture, faucets, lighting, and more. It offers a unique opportunity to scale projects and achieve new objectives by interacting and connecting with suppliers, professionals, and industry leaders.

item.title: Pavilion in Brolo Park / CN10 architetti
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The construction of the new pavilion is part of a larger urban project to reclaim and enhance a large green space called PARCOBROLO, which extends to the southern part of the town of Bonate Sotto in the Villa district, covering an area of over 30,000 square meters. This large orchard (brolo) has survived over time, untouched by the expansion of the surrounding buildings.

item.title: Public Interest Design in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: This book presents salient examples of architectural projects and practices in South Africa since 1994 that collectively subscribe to the paradigm shift towards Public Interest Design. Despite radical political transformation in the country, the people of South Africa remain adversely affected by the socio-spatial legacies of a segregated urban landscape. The contributions by architects to address these challenges go largely unnoticed and remain a marginalised practice, even within the mainstream profession.

item.title: Call for Proposals: Bahrain Pavilion at the Venice Architecture Biennale 2027
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: The Bahrain Authority for Culture and Antiquities invites individuals and collaborative teams to submit proposals to represent the National Pavilion of Bahrain at the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, taking place from 8 May to 21 November 2027, with pre-opening on 6 and 7 May.

item.title: Metaxis: A Collection of Ideas and Objects by FUTUREFORMS
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
This exhibition takes as its point of departure the Greek word metaxi, referring to an in‑between condition—belonging to two realms at once. METAXIS explores what happens in between: between ideas, objects, spaces, and ways of seeing. It reflects on the dynamic state of being in the middle of things, a shifting tension or oscillation rather than a fixed condition. The exhibited projects move fluidly between perception and imagination, inside and outside, presence and absence, art and architecture. What does it mean to create public art and architecture in the 21st century?

item.title: Cinema Studio Namibe: Reviving a Tropical Modernist Icon in Angola
item.dc:creator: Camilla Ghisleni
item.description: What sustains the purpose of architecture that has never been occupied? For decades, this was the question surrounding the Namibe Cinema-Studio, built on the coast of Angola in 1973. Conceived as a film screening venue, the building remained closed and abandoned, never fulfilling the role for which it was created. Yet it withstood the passage of time, becoming an icon of the Angolan landscape and architecture, until finally screening its first film nearly fifty years later.
